views.caption: Seed 7, star 33, night 1: a held tracking drift, a cosmic ray, a hot pixel and an end-of-night flare on one curve. Only the field detector names the drift.

Seed 7 over 20 nights, star 185, night 6: a 1.4% dip over five and a half hours on a star whose noise is 1.7% per sample. No per-night detector sees it; bls finds it by folding the star's whole record and bounds it on each of its three nights.

Seed 7 over 20 nights, star 93, night 9: a planet that transits once in the whole survey, already under way when the night starts. single_transit bounds it as a box truncated by the night edge; a periodic search cannot, because there is no second event.

Seed 22 over 20 nights, star 6, night 3: a 2.1% planet transit in the middle of the night, on a star that also pulsates by 0.8%. The pulsation is smaller than the 1.4% scatter of each sample, and the per-night detectors report nothing. bls and single_transit each subtract the pulsation before searching, and both bound the transit.
Seed 42, star 24, night 2: median_residual's two fragments inside a flare it had already bounded were booked as false alarms until the scorer learned to call them corroborating.
Seed 7, star 7, night 1: the tracking drift as the field detector sees it, spanning an hour past the ramp because its causal baseline absorbs the step.

findings.text: Before any detector was wrong, the scorer was: a simple detector looked like it made 312 false alarms, but 281 of them overlapped real events, and once the scoring rules were fixed the same detections gave 34.

Before building a search for repeating dips, the project counted what a 3-night survey holds: only 1 of 34 planets in one run and 1 of 25 in the other transited more than once, with a combined signal of just 0.1 and 1.7 against a bar of 7, so it surveyed 20 nights instead.

A fix that worked on the sky it was built on did nothing on six skies it had never seen (seeds 21 to 26) and raised false alarms from 6 to 9, so it shipped switched off and unseen "held-out" seeds became a standing rule.
A gate that would have removed 28 false claims was shipped switched off, because it would also have lost 18 real transits that the project's other transit search could not find.

Dividing every star by the field's median cancels sky-wide effects, but when most stars pulsate the median is itself a wobble that gets written into every star, and fixing that cut one run's false planet claims from 14 to 2.

A cause written down for a lost planet was invented by a side script that prepared the star differently from the real detector, and on the detector's own path the star's one candidate was dropped by a shape test at 1.57 against a bar of 1.0.

Even when told a planet's exact period and duration, the periodic search reads its dip at a median 0.65 of the ideal signal, and about 70% of that loss is the honest price of comparing the dip with the rest of its own night; the one fix that looked possible gained nothing on unseen runs, so it was closed.

honesty.text: The simulator writes the truth when it injects each event, and the detectors never see it; only the scorer does.
A change is designed on development seeds and scored once on unseen seeds, only after every threshold is committed; the one time a gate was set after seeing unseen data, build log 0012 says so.

Every code pull request is reviewed by a second agent that breaks the code one defect at a time and checks the tests catch each break, and since build log 0011 every bar is written in planets, with an allowance of one planet.

A bar is written before the unseen seeds are scored and is never loosened afterwards: a change that misses it is closed, or ships with the miss written down as a cost set against what it measurably gained.
